tries.before: Ads, screens, fear and cravings are already training your mind, and so are your tribe, the people in authority, loneliness and plain old repetition. With self-hypnosis you can train your own mind from the inside, by befriending and listening to the deeper part of your mind. This opens up a whole new area of choice for you as an adult in the world.
tries.after: With self-hypnosis you can train your own mind from the inside, by befriending and listening to the deeper part of your mind. This opens up a whole new area of choice for you as an adult in the world.

tries.where: Let the response change the invitation, P1
tries.before: Your shoulders tightening, or 'hmm, that feels kind of wrong', is a signal to investigate further. A tightening won't tell you what it's about by itself, so ask what happened and whether the invitation fits. But 'No! That is Not Right!' is a signal to stop what you're doing and change it. If you don't feel like it fits, don't keep doing it, and don't try saying it again more persuasively. Just change it. You don't need any other reason.
tries.after: Your shoulders tightening, or 'hmm, that feels kind of wrong', is a signal to investigate further, but 'No! That is Not Right!' is a signal to stop what you're doing and change it. If you don't feel like it fits, don't keep doing it, and don't try saying it again more persuasively. Just change it. You don't need any other reason.
tries.why: On 28 October I found this point said already (AUDIT.md, F6a.1): the response check just above calls a tightness a notice, not a meaning, and says to find out what happened, and the script just below asks whether the invitation fits. My restored sentence said it again and read AI. The sentence goes back to one, as it read High on 29 October; "don't try saying it again more persuasively" stays.

tries.where: Let the response change the invitation, P3
tries.before: Sometimes the invitation just isn't right. Sometimes it brings up a possibility you hadn't thought of, and the feeling that comes with it is worth meeting. You don't have to know which it is before you make room to find out. Either way, your doubt isn't automatically a guard, and silence doesn't mean a hidden process is working.
tries.after: Sometimes the invitation just isn't right, and other times it's brought up something you hadn't thought of, with a feeling that's worth meeting, so give it a little room and find out which. Either way, your doubt isn't automatically a guard, and silence doesn't mean a hidden process is working.
tries.why: My clear version read AI (High): two "Sometimes" sentences in a row, a "you don't have to" line and a tidy pair. This keeps every point in two sentences, the shape of the unclear version that read High on 29 October.

tries.before: Let your response guide you as to what to do next regardless of what the script is expecting. Utilize: use what you have (a thought, sound, movement, or objection) to go to the next place, whatever it is. Learn how to notice what is there. If nothing changes, notice that too: no change doesn't mean it worked in some way you can't see. For more on language you can use, see Appendix B, or keep reading below for information on using the tools after induction in Let the next response guide you. Either way, keep the instructions about how to stay safe and how to get out plain.

tries.read: AI (Medium and Low), part B windows 9 and 11
tries.before: A presupposition is an assumption hidden inside a sentence. Presumption is a powerful thing, so please don’t use it except to presume that we will have the choice of when it will happen, that we will be able to do it, that we are safe, that we are loved and that our adult can lead us. Never use it to sneak in obedience.
tries.after: Presumption is a powerful thing (a presupposition hides an assumption inside a sentence, and the person hearing it usually takes that assumption on board), so please don’t use it except to presume that we will have the choice of when it will happen, that we will be able to do it, that we are safe, that we are loved and that our adult can lead us. Don’t ever presume obedience, the way a hypnotist does when they say something like, ‘As you go deeper, it gets easier and easier to just do what I say.’
tries.why: Read AI: a textbook definition on its own and a short command. This puts the definition inside the sentence you approved, as an aside that says why presumption is powerful, and shows what presuming obedience sounds like, the way your reframing paragraph shows the dishonest reframe before the honest one.

tries.read: AI (High), part B window 15 (it ran on into your embedded-invitations paragraph)
tries.before: Bridge words are words like ‘as, whilst, because, when, after, before, which means’ etc. These are words that link events. However, even if you say them in a lovely gentle voice it doesn’t mean that it’s true if it isn’t! It’s not very likely that just by breathing in and out your trauma is going to go away! A better bridge claims a lot less: ‘As I breathe, my adult self may become present enough to hear a small piece of what the wound needs.’
tries.after: Bridge words are words like ‘as, whilst, because, when, after, before, which means’ etc. These are words that link events. However, even if you say them in a lovely gentle voice it doesn’t mean that it’s true if it isn’t! It’s not very likely that just by breathing in and out your trauma is going to go away! So an honest bridge might sound more like, ‘As I breathe, my adult self may become present enough to hear a little of what the wound needs.’
tries.why: "A better bridge claims a lot less:" was a colon reveal, and the red ran on into your paragraph after it. This leads into the better version the way your reframing paragraph does ("So we might arrive at, ...").
